name: NIQE Quality Score
description: Computes Natural Image Quality Evaluator blind quality score — AI images often score differently from natural photos (Mittal et al., 2013).
mechanism:
This method implements the Natural Image Quality Evaluator (NIQE) by Mittal et al. (2013) for blind quality assessment:

1. **NSS Feature Extraction**: The image is decomposed into normalized luminance coefficients using mean-subtracted contrast-normalized (MSCN) coefficients: Î(x,y) = (I(x,y) − μ(x,y))/(σ(x,y) + C). These MSCN coefficients of natural images follow a unit Gaussian distribution.

2. **Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD) Fitting**: MSCN coefficient distributions are fit to a GGD parameterized by shape (α) and variance (σ²). Additionally, pairwise products of adjacent MSCN coefficients are modeled using an asymmetric GGD (AGGD) in four directions (horizontal, vertical, and two diagonals).

3. **Multivariate Gaussian (MVG) Model**: The extracted NSS features (GGD shape, variance, AGGD parameters) form a feature vector. A pristine MVG model (μₙ, Σₙ) is pre-computed from a corpus of natural undistorted images.

4. **Quality Distance Computation**: The NIQE score is computed as the Mahalanobis-like distance: D = √((μ₁−μ₂)ᵀ((Σ₁+Σ₂)/2)⁻¹(μ₁−μ₂)) between the test image's feature distribution (μ₁, Σ₁) and the pristine model (μ₂, Σ₂). Lower scores indicate more natural-looking images.

5. **Forensic Application**: AI-generated images often deviate from natural scene statistics (NSS) captured by NIQE. While visually plausible, synthetic images exhibit subtle violations of NSS regularity — particularly in local contrast normalization and adjacent coefficient dependencies — yielding elevated NIQE scores that serve as a generation indicator.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Mittal, A. et al. (2013). Making a Completely Blind Image Quality Analyzer. IEEE Signal Processing Letters.
Mittal, A. et al. (2012). No-Reference Image Quality Assessment in the Spatial Domain. IEEE TIP.
